questions.stem: What is Data Observability primarily about?
options: Observing every data pipeline, transformation and policy across the organisation and providing analysis for decision making
Encrypting data in transit between data stores
Replacing data governance with automated monitoring
Archiving old data pipelines that are no longer used
Designing the physical schema of a data warehouse
questions.explanation: Data Observability observes pipelines, transformations, DDL, DML, governance standards and security and privacy policies to build a holistic view that supports decision making.

questions.stem: Under which discipline does Data Observability sit?
options: Master Data Management
Network Security
Business Intelligence
Metadata Management
Data Warehousing
questions.explanation: Data Observability comes under Metadata Management, since it works mainly by observing enterprise metadata.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the five pillars of Data Observability?
options: Freshness
Lineage
Encryption
Volume
Distribution
questions.explanation: The five pillars are Freshness, Lineage, Schema, Volume and Distribution; encryption is not among them.

questions.stem: What kind of data does Data Observability mainly access in order to do its work?
options: Raw transactional data in production databases
Enterprise metadata
Customer survey responses
Financial ledgers
Backup tapes and archives
questions.explanation: Rather than needing access to every framework, Data Observability mainly accesses enterprise metadata through the Metadata Management tools.

questions.stem: Why can a Data Observability framework realistically be granted access across an enterprise despite security and audit concerns?
options: Because it runs only outside business hours
Because it is operated by the Audit department itself
Because it reads data only in test environments
Because it stores nothing it observes
Because access is requested only on the tools used for Metadata Management
questions.explanation: Security, Risk, Compliance and Audit would not allow one framework access to all frameworks, but access limited to Metadata Management tools is acceptable.

questions.stem: Which departments are named as unlikely to allow one framework access to every framework in the enterprise?
options: Marketing, Sales, Finance and HR
Data Science, Analytics, BI and Reporting
Security, Risk, Compliance and Audit
Procurement, Legal, Facilities and Operations
Development, Testing, Release and Support
questions.explanation: Security, Risk, Compliance and Audit are the departments that would block blanket access, which is why Data Observability targets metadata instead.

questions.stem: When does Data Observability look at sample data rather than metadata?
options: On request, for debugging purposes
Continuously, for every table in every data store
Only during the annual audit
Never; it is forbidden from reading any sample data
Only when the data is already encrypted
questions.explanation: Data Observability normally observes metadata, and looks at sample data only on request when debugging is needed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed among the things Data Observability observes?
options: Metadata of all tables in all data stores
ETL and ELT tools and shell scripts
Dashboards, reports, code sets and KPIs
Customer payment card numbers stored in production tables
All the logs
questions.explanation: Data Observability observes metadata, upstream and downstream data stores, dashboards, ETL and ELT tools, scripts and logs; it does not observe sensitive production values such as card numbers.

questions.stem: What makes enterprise-wide Data Observability a challenge in most IT environments?
options: Metadata is too small to be useful
Frameworks sit in silos across many clusters, network segments, zones and environments behind firewalls with no centralised control
Most organisations have no data pipelines to observe
Data Observability tools cannot read logs
Business users refuse to look at dashboards
questions.explanation: Without centralised control, the many silos, clusters, network zones and firewalls make it hard to observe everything from one place.

questions.stem: With what in place is enterprise Data Observability ideally achievable?
options: A single relational database for all systems
A dedicated Security Operations Centre
A monthly manual audit of all pipelines
A cloud-only infrastructure
A Data and AI Cognitive (DAC) Architecture
questions.explanation: Ideally, enterprise Data Observability is possible when a Data and AI Cognitive (DAC) Architecture is in place.
